'''''Galium album''''', [[common name]]s '''white bedstraw'''<ref name=plantsdb>{{Cite PLANTS | symbol=GAAL | taxon=Galium album | access-date = 9 December 2024}}</ref> and '''upright hedge bedstraw''',<ref name=eppo>{{cite web | title = ''Galium album'' | url = https://gd.eppo.int/taxon/GALAL | publisher = [[European and Mediterranean Plant Protection Organization]] (EPPO) | access-date = 9 December 2024}}</ref> is an [[annual plant|annual]], [[herbaceous plant]] of the family [[Rubiaceae]] and is native to much of Europe.

==Description==
The stems can grow to at least {{Convert|150|cm|ft|abbr=off|0}} and are more or less erect with ascending branches. The stem is square in sections with slight [[flange]]s. The plant is relatively hairless with shiny leaves and stem. Flowers are white or yellowish.<ref name="CTW">Clapham, A. R., Tutin, T. G. and Warburg, E. F. (1987). ''Excursion Flora of the British Isles.'' Cambridge: Cambridge University Press. {{ISBN|0-521-23290-2}}. p. 302.</ref> The fruits are hairless.<ref>Hennedy, Roger (1891). ''The Clydesdale Flora''. Glasgow: Hugh Hopkins. p. 97.</ref><ref>Michalková, Eleonóra. 1993. Biología, Bot. (Bratislava) 48(1): 48</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
''Galium album'' is widespread over much of Europe, native to a large region from Britain to Morocco, east to Turkey and Western Siberia. It has been introduced and is naturalized in Ireland, Scandinavia, Greenland and South Australia.<ref name=powo/> It is found in pastures and grassy banks, especially on dry calcareous soils. In Britain, ''G. album'' is local in lowland England, rare in the north, and very rare in Scotland.<ref name="CTW"/>

==Subspecies==
Five subspecies were accepted by [[Plants of the World Online]] {{as of|2024|December|lc=y}}, listed here with their native distributions:<ref name=powo/>
*''Galium album'' subsp. ''album'' – most of the range of the species<ref name=powoalbum>{{Cite POWO | id =77168429-1 | title =''Galium album'' subsp. ''album'' | access-date = 9 December 2024}}</ref>
*''Galium album'' subsp. ''amani'' <small>Ehrend. & Schönb.-Tem.</small> – parts of Lebanon, Syria, and Turkey<ref name=powoamani>{{Cite POWO | id =890264-1 | title =''Galium album'' subsp. ''amani'' Ehrend. & Schönb.-Tem. | access-date = 9 December 2024}}</ref>
*''Galium album ''subsp. ''prusense'' <small>(K.Koch) Ehrend. & Krendl</small> – Greece, Bulgaria, Crimea, Turkey, and Caucasus<ref name=powoprusense>{{Cite POWO | id =890266-1 | title =''Galium album'' subsp. ''prusense'' (K.Koch) Ehrend. & Krendl | access-date = 9 December 2024}}</ref>
*''Galium album'' subsp. ''pycnotrichum'' <small>(Heinr.Braun) Krendl</small> – from Poland south to Greece and Turkey<ref name=powopycnotrichum>{{Cite POWO | id =77189441-1 | title = ''Galium album'' subsp. ''pycnotrichum'' (Heinr.Braun) Krendl | access-date = 9 December 2024}}</ref>
*''Galium album ''subsp''. suberectum'' <small>(Klokov) Michalk.</small> – Carpathian Mountains of western Ukraine<ref name=powosuberectum>{{Cite POWO | id = 975731-1 | title = ''Galium album'' subsp. ''suberectum'' (Klokov) Michalk. | access-date = 9 December 2024}}</ref>
